answer.rationale: The 18% spend cut and 14-day expiration window create urgency, but the 94% assembly line utilization is a hard constraint—switching vendors or adding a second source carry execution risk in this timeframe. Renegotiation offers the fastest path to cost reduction while preserving the incumbent relationship and delivery stability that has proven reliable across two cycles. Pulling memory_c4 validates whether benchmarking pressure worked before and is repeatable; pulling memory_c2 confirms whether vendor switching timelines are feasible given current line stress. The durable record shows negotiation recovered real margin at renewal (c4) and multi-year commitments unlocked volume pricing (c6). With 14 days, aggressive renegotiation—anchored to the market data that moved the incumbent previously—is lower-risk than sourcing alternatives. This preserves optionality: if negotiation fails, deferral to month-to-month (following c5 precedent) protects budget flexibility while buying time for a staged second source or vendor transition in a less stressed operational window.
